content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Model underestimates prices during periods of strong upward momentum, particularly when true values rise sharply after a dip.
- Model tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast.
- Overshoots occur after sharp price increases, leading to inflated forecasts that fail to capture subsequent mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the second half of the forecast, especially when true values show downward correction.
- Mean reversion is under-predicted — model fails to anticipate price pullback after peaks, leading to over-optimistic later forecasts.
- Forecasts are overly sensitive to recent volatility, often overreacting to short-term noise rather than underlying trend.
